records.name: Auseklis
records.facts_used: Auseklis: The Latvian personal name is connected with auseklis, the morning star. The word occurs in mythological and poetic language as well as personal names. A reference to the celestial object or figure does not itself date the first child bearing this given name. Poet Miķelis Krogzemis used the literary name Auseklis. The National Encyclopaedia dates the start of his publishing to 1872. This is a dated literary-name example, rather than his birth given name.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Siliņš p75 morning-star formation; PaulsDaija signed encyclopaedia confirms poet real name and 1872start publishing. No decorative-symbol firstdate inferred.

records.name: Alfredas
records.facts_used: Alfredas: The Lithuanian form continues the Alfred family from Old English Ælfræd. The compound contains ælf, elf, and ræd, counsel. These explain the old formation; the poetic combination does not assert a historical instance of advice from elves. Related Alfred was borne by Swedish inventor Alfred Nobel (1833–1896), associated with the foundation of the Nobel Prizes. This is a dated foreign family example, rather than the first Lithuanian registration of Alfredas.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Exact guide and curated Lithuanian variant Alfredas/Ælfræd stems. Dated related foreign namesake Nobel 1833–1896 explicitly scoped.
